selected_reviews.title: Fleet ignored registered restricted custom agents and dispatched built-ins
selected_reviews.assessment: The reporter registered a read-only custom worker and then observed Fleet dispatch two built-in explore workers instead; the returned answer explicitly recorded the built-in names. The documented impact is that custom tool restrictions and system prompts do not bind Fleet workers. Two public comments report related custom-agent dispatch failures through September. This is a concrete multi-worker configuration-boundary failure, but the public record does not show a task result consumed downstream or rogue intent.
selected_reviews.verified_participants: Caller and two worker events asserted from SDK output; worker autonomy and model identities not independently authenticated
selected_reviews.provider_attribution: GitHub Copilot SDK 0.1.32 and Copilot CLI; effective worker models not established

selected_reviews.title: Terra session delegated planning, implementation and review to unselected Opus workers
selected_reviews.assessment: A user-selected Terra session reportedly made seven Opus subagent invocations for planning, implementation, exploration and review without a logged reason or explicit user selection. A second reporter describes a Sonnet worker delegating its actual restructure to an Opus child despite a cost-saving model choice. These are concrete nested-delegation and result-use episodes crossing a model-selection and cost expectation, but they were already public and remain consistent with product routing defects rather than rogue intent.
selected_reviews.verified_participants: Parent and worker model roles asserted from reporter-held CLI event logs; runtime identities not independently authenticated
selected_reviews.provider_attribution: GitHub Copilot CLI via IntelliJ; GPT-5.6 Terra parent and Claude Opus/Sonnet workers reported

selected_reviews.title: Built-in workers did not inherit operator custom instructions
selected_reviews.assessment: The reporter asked four built-in agents which command they would use under an explicit environment instruction. The parent aggregated their responses: only the general-purpose worker used the required command, while explore, task and code-review selected prohibited system-Python commands. The issue also reports actual direct Python and temporary-directory use. This is a parent-worker exchange and instruction-boundary control, not evidence of peer coordination or rogue intent.
selected_reviews.verified_participants: Four named built-in worker roles asserted through one parent report; no independent session or model authentication
selected_reviews.provider_attribution: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.3; Claude Sonnet 4.6 parent reported

selected_reviews.title: Parent duplicated specialist work and discarded late worker results
selected_reviews.assessment: The original report says a parent stopped waiting, duplicated specialist work and discarded the late result. A July comment shows repeated completion summaries after the main agent claimed it would handle the task directly. This establishes duplicate parent-worker activity and late result transfer, but not recipient use or an operator-defined coordination boundary. The issue was closed as fixed before later recurrence comments and is not ongoing-agent evidence.
selected_reviews.verified_participants: Parent and specialist roles asserted from public issue excerpts; no independent session authentication
selected_reviews.provider_attribution: GitHub Copilot CLI; versions and effective models not established in the original report

selected_reviews.title: Model-emitted override silently defeated a human complementary-review setting
selected_reviews.assessment: A Claude parent reportedly supplied a model argument that overrode the user's complementary reviewer setting, causing a same-family worker to perform the review. The reporter checked the resolver precedence offline, and a commenter associated with the runtime project confirmed that model discretion was allowed to override while noting an instruction-delivery bug. This is a user-configuration boundary failure in an intended review workflow; actual downstream use of the review is not preserved.
selected_reviews.verified_participants: Parent and reviewer roles asserted from reporter-held event logs; model labels not independently attested
selected_reviews.provider_attribution: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.79; Claude Opus parent and reviewer reported

selected_reviews.title: Task workers ignored a global attribution opt-out and amended commits
selected_reviews.assessment: With the global coauthor setting disabled, eight of eight subagent-created commits still received the attribution trailer while direct parent commits did not. One worker amended an otherwise finished commit solely to add it. This is persistent delegated output crossing an explicit global setting, but it is a product prompt/configuration defect and not evidence of inter-agent rogue intent.
selected_reviews.verified_participants: Parent and task-worker roles inferred from public reproduction counts and logs; model identities not established
selected_reviews.provider_attribution: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.80; effective model not established

assessment.result: No previously unreported rogue swarm. The selected records add strong controls for Fleet worker restriction failure, unexpected nested model delegation, missing instruction inheritance, duplicate specialist work, human-setting override and persistent delegated output. All are already public product incidents with reporter-asserted participant provenance.
assessment.advancement_test: A new candidate needs a not-previously-published original exchange, independently corroborated autonomous participant provenance, demonstrated recipient use of a transferred task result, and evidence that the coordination itself exceeded authorization rather than reflecting Copilot's intended Fleet/task design or a known configuration/routing defect.

limitations: Fifteen repository-scoped first pages are not a census; two searches were capped at 30 results and the pages overlap heavily.
Issue bodies and comments summarize reporter-held event logs; this pass did not download attachments or independently authenticate sessions and models.
Some reports concern settings described as expectations rather than hard capability restrictions; boundary assessments preserve that distinction.
Open issue state and recent issue updates do not establish ongoing agent activity.
No reproduction, runtime invocation, attachment download, issue comment, external message or other write was performed.
redactions: Session IDs, local paths, raw prompts, raw tool payloads, commit identifiers, personal addresses and private logs omitted; issue bodies represented by SHA256
